mainTopic: רבי יוחנן's rulings on one who falsely claims 'a thief took it' (טוען טענת גנב): ארבעה וחמשה, a lost item, and the need for a partial admission
overview: The amud opens by finishing a difficulty about רב's view. If witnesses cannot make a false swearer pay, how can a later oath bring a קרבן just because he might admit someday? Then רבי חייא בר אבא quotes a series of rulings from רבי יוחנן about a שומר who falsely claims 'a thief took it'. First, such a person pays כפל, and if he slaughtered or sold the animal he pays ארבעה וחמשה like a real גנב. This is learned from a היקש or from the extra ה in 'הַגַּנָּב'. A ברייתא where he ate the ox and paid only כפל is explained as a case where he ate it as a נבילה, and the גמרא explains why the other possible answers were not used. Second, a finder who falsely claims a lost item was stolen also pays כפל. This is challenged from a ברייתא about a minor's deposit and answered in two ways, by רבי חייא בר אבא and by רב אשי. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that the false thief claim makes him liable only if he admits part of the claim and denies part, based on 'כִּי הוּא זֶה'. The גמרא notes that רבי חייא בר יוסף disagrees, and his view comes on the next amud.

steps.title: If witnesses make him liable, the extra oaths make sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that if a false swearer has to pay once witnesses come, it is easy to see why each later oath brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine if you say that when he swore and then witnesses came, he has to pay. That is why we make him bring a קרבן for the last oath: he can still go back and admit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. First it shows the side of the argument that works well, before showing the side that does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say witnesses can still make him pay after his first false oath. Then he still owes money, and if he admits he will have to pay. So each new false oath is again a false denial of money he owes, and that is why it brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well; this opens the side that makes sense, before the side that has a problem.
He is liable, meaning he has to pay.
The קרבן brought for swearing falsely to deny money (an אשם).
The later one, here the last oath.
He can still go back and admit.

phrases.english: It works out fine if you say: he swore,
and when witnesses come, he is liable;
that is why we obligate him
to bring a קרבן for the later oath,
phrases.notes: This refers to a case where he swore the same false oath again and again, and he brings a קרבן for each one.

phrases.english: since he can go back and admit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a difficulty already under way about רב's view, which began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a false swearer is exempt even when witnesses come
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the 'it works fine' half. The ruling that every oath brings a קרבן fits a view in which witnesses make him liable.

steps.title: If witnesses do not make him liable, why bring a קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: If even witnesses cannot make him pay, there is no good reason to demand a קרבן for later oaths just because he might admit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that when witnesses come he is exempt, is there anything like this? If witnesses came and testified against him, he would be exempt. Yet we would require a קרבן for his oath just because he could admit? Right now, at least, he has not admitted!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual punch of the challenge against רב's view: the 'he could admit' reason falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose witnesses cannot make him pay after his oath. Then right now he owes nothing. A later oath is not denying any real debt, so it should not bring a קרבן. The idea that 'he might admit someday' is too weak, because he has not admitted yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt; he does not have to pay.
Is there any such thing? This is a question meant to show that the idea makes no sense.
Witnesses (the Aramaic word for עדים).
Now, at any rate.
He admitted.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'liabilities'. One is paying money after witnesses come. The other is bringing a קרבן for a false oath. The question is whether the קרבן can exist when the money obligation does not.

phrases.english: But if you say
that when witnesses come he is exempt,
phrases.notes: This is רב's view, which the גמרא was discussing before this point.

phrases.english: is there any such thing

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ אָתוּ סָהֲדִי וּמַסְהֲדִי בֵּיהּ – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: where, if witnesses came and testified against him, he would be exempt,
and yet we would stand up and obligate him
to bring a קרבן for an oath
because he can go back and admit?!
Right now, at any rate, he has not admitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the 'it works fine' setup of step 1 into a challenge against the opposite view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that witnesses do not make the false swearer liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קרבן שבועה requires denying money he actually owes. If even witnesses could not make him pay, he owes nothing now, and a possible future admission cannot create a debt today.
steps.whatToRemember: A קרבן for a false oath only makes sense if the swearer still really owes the money at that moment.

steps.title: Falsely claiming 'a thief took it' brings כפל and ארבעה וחמשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a שומר who falsely claims a thief stole the deposit pays כפל. If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays four or five times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who makes the claim 'a thief took it' about a deposit pays double. If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: a new ruling by רבי יוחנן about a שומר who lies that the deposit was stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already says that a שומר who falsely claims 'it was stolen' pays כפל, just like a thief. רבי יוחנן adds something new: if he also slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays the full ארבעה וחמשה penalty that a real גנב pays.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes the claim 'a thief stole it'.
A deposit left with a שומר for safekeeping.
Double payment, the fine a thief pays.
He slaughtered or sold the animal.
Fourfold payment (for a sheep) or fivefold payment (for an ox).

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'false thief-claimer' is treated as a real גנב in every respect, not only for כפל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
one who claims, about a deposit, that a thief took it
phrases.notes: He means this claim turned out to be a lie, and he actually took it himself.

phrases.english: pays double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion on the related topic of a שומר who falsely claims theft.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false 'a thief took it' claimer pays כפל, and if he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Why: he is compared to a real thief
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that since both pay כפל, the false claimer is just like a גנב and also pays ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a thief pays double, and the false thief-claimer also pays double, we compare them. A thief who pays double pays four or five times if he slaughtered or sold. So too, the false thief-claimer, who pays double, pays four or five times if he slaughtered or sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the reason for his ruling by comparing the false claimer to a real thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared point is כפל: the Torah made both of them pay double. Since the Torah treats them the same for כפל, רבי יוחנן extends the comparison to the next penalty, ארבעה וחמשה, which for a real thief comes on top of כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; it introduces the shared feature that the comparison is built on.
Just as ... so too; the standard way of comparing two cases.
A thief.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, whoever pays כפל like a גנב also pays ארבעה וחמשה like a גנב.

phrases.english: Since a thief pays double payment,

phrases.aramaic: וְטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל –
phrases.english: and one who claims 'a thief took it' pays double payment,
then just as a thief, who pays double,

phrases.aramaic: טָבַח וּמָכַר מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה;
phrases.english: pays fourfold or fivefold payment if he slaughtered or sold,
so too one who claims, about a deposit, that a thief took it,
since he pays double payment,

phrases.aramaic: טָבַח וּמָכַר מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: pays fourfold or fivefold payment if he slaughtered or sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the false thief-claimer pays ארבעה וחמשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to a real גנב, based on the shared כפל payment

steps.title: A real thief is stricter, so how can we learn from him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's comparison. A גנב pays כפל even without a שבועה, but a טוען טענת גנב pays כפל only after a false שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a thief? He is special because he pays double even without an oath. Would you say the same about someone who falsely claims a thief stole the deposit, who pays double only after swearing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's logic from Step 4. It points out that a real גנב is stricter than a טוען טענת גנב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the two are alike because both pay כפל. But the גנב pays כפל with no oath at all, while the טוען טענת גנב pays it only after a false שבועה. Since the גנב is stricter, his extra penalty of ארבעה וחמשה should not carry over to the weaker case.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about...?" A way of showing that one case has a special stringency the other case lacks
Double payment
Oath
A שומר who falsely claims that a thief stole the deposit

phrases.english: What about a thief? He is special because he pays
double payment even without an oath.
Will you say the same about one who claims a thief took it,
who does not pay double payment
except after an oath?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְגַנָּב – שֶׁכֵּן מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison רבי יוחנן made in Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reasoning that a טוען טענת גנב is just like a גנב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case (a גנב) has an extra stringency, paying כפל without an oath, so its further penalty cannot be carried over to a weaker case

steps.title: It is a היקש, which cannot be refuted
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבי יוחנן did not use logic. He used a היקש, and a היקש cannot be challenged with a "מה ל" argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: it is a juxtaposition, and one cannot argue against a juxtaposition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יוחנן's rule comes from a היקש, not from a logical comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A "מה ל" challenge only works against reasoning, such as a קל וחומר. A היקש is a teaching built into the way the תורה places the פסוקים, so pointing out differences between the cases does not break it.

keyTerms.meaning: "They say": introduces the answer
A teaching learned because the תורה places two cases next to each other
We do not argue against it or refute it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא admits the cases are equal. It agrees they differ, but says a היקש works even when the cases differ.

phrases.english: They say: it is a juxtaposition,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוקים about a thief and about one who claims a thief took the deposit sit right next to each other.

phrases.english: and one does not refute a juxtaposition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הֶיקֵּישָׁא הִיא, וְאֵין מְשִׁיבִין עַל הֶיקֵּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasts the source of the ruling: it comes from a היקש, not from logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן was reasoning from similarity, which a difference can break
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from a היקש, which cannot be refuted by pointing out differences

steps.title: What if both פסוקים speak about the false claimer?
steps.stepSummary: The היקש answer works for the view that one פסוק speaks about a גנב and one about a טוען טענת גנב. But one view holds that both פסוקים speak about a טוען טענת גנב. Then there is no היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says one פסוק is about a thief and one is about a false claimer. But according to the one who says both "if the thief is found" and "if he is not found" are about a false claimer, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the היקש answer from Step 6. According to one opinion, there is no פסוק about a real גנב here to compare with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש needs two different cases placed side by side. If both פסוקים speak only about the טוען טענת גנב, nothing links him to a real גנב. So the answer of Step 6 fails for that opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: "This works well": introduces a view that fits, before raising one that does not
According to the one who says
Both of them
What is there to say? A standard challenge

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: חַד בְּגַנָּב וְחַד בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב, שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: one is about a thief and one is about a false claimer of theft; that is fine.
But according to the one who says
that this, "If the thief shall be found,"
and "If he shall not be found"
both are about a false claimer of theft,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר חַד בְּגַנָּב וְחַד בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the היקש answer of Step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both פסוקים deal only with the טוען טענת גנב, no פסוק about a real גנב sits next to his case, so there is no היקש

steps.title: The extra letter in "הַגַּנָּב" teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said "גנב" but says "הגנב". The extra ה includes the טוען טענת גנב in the thief's ארבעה וחמשה rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: "thief" versus "the thief."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even without a היקש, the rule is learned from the extra letter ה in the word "הַגַּנָּב".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if no פסוק links the two cases side by side, the extra letter ה adds something. It teaches that the false claimer is treated like a real גנב for ארבעה וחמשה. So רבי יוחנן's ruling stands according to both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: "The thief": the word with the extra letter ה that teaches the rule

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule that a טוען טענת גנב pays ארבעה וחמשה is not built on logic, which could be refuted. It comes from the פסוקים: either a היקש, or the extra ה in "הַגַּנָּב".

phrases.english: They say: "thief" versus "the thief."
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have just said "thief". The extra ה ("the") comes to include the false claimer too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides a new source: an extra letter in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a היקש, there seemed to be no source for this opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra ה in "הַגַּנָּב" includes the טוען טענת גנב in the ארבעה וחמשה rule

steps.title: A ברייתא where the false claimer who ate the ox pays only double
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא brings a ברייתא. A שומר swore falsely that the ox was stolen, and witnesses say he ate it. He pays only כפל. Eating requires שחיטה, so why does he not pay ארבעה וחמשה, as רבי יוחנן said?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא challenged רבי יוחנן: "Where is my ox?" "It was stolen." "I make you swear." He said "Amen." Then witnesses testify that he ate it. He pays double. But here, you cannot eat even a כזית of meat without שחיטה, and still it teaches that he pays double. Double, yes. Four and five, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, the false claimer seems to have slaughtered the animal, yet he pays only כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To eat an animal, you normally slaughter it first. So in the ברייתא the שומר must have slaughtered the ox. If רבי יוחנן is right, he should pay ארבעה וחמשה, but the ברייתא lists only כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a written source (a משנה or ברייתא)
It was stolen (the שומר's false claim)
I make you swear (the owner demands a שבועה)
Amen; answering this accepts the oath as if he said it himself
An olive-size amount, the smallest amount that counts as eating
Kosher slaughter

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
"Where is my ox?" "It was stolen."
phrases.notes: The owner is asking the שומר who was watching his ox, and the שומר gives a false answer.

phrases.english: "I make you swear," and he said: "Amen,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he ate it,
he pays double payment.
But here, where it is impossible
to have even an olive-size of meat without slaughtering,
and it teaches: he pays double payment;
double payment, yes,
fourfold and fivefold payment, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's ruling is secured, through the היקש or the extra ה of הגנב, the גמרא brings a new challenge to it from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a טוען טענת גנב pays ארבעה וחמשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating means slaughter took place, yet the ברייתא gives only כפל. This implies no ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: He ate it as a נבילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where he killed the ox without proper שחיטה and ate it as a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where he ate it as a נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. He says the ברייתא is about a case where there was no kosher שחיטה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 assumed that eating means he slaughtered properly. The answer says he killed it some other way and ate the נבילה. Without real שחיטה, there is no ארבעה וחמשה, so only כפל applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow down a source)
For example; such as
An animal that died or was killed without kosher שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Eating a נבילה is forbidden, but the ברייתא is describing what the שומר actually did, not what he was allowed to do.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Such as where he ate it as an unslaughtered carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating the ox means he slaughtered it properly.
steps.terutzMaskana: He ate it as a נבילה with no kosher שחיטה, so only כפל applies.

steps.title: Why not say he ate it as a טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not answer that the ox was a טריפה, slaughtered but still not permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him answer instead: such as where he ate it as a טריפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן picked the answer of נבילה. It offers another answer: the animal was a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a טריפה, the שחיטה does not make the meat kosher. The suggestion is that such a שחיטה might not count as real שחיטה for ארבעה וחמשה. That would also explain why only כפל is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him answer him (with a different answer)
An animal with a fatal defect; even proper שחיטה does not make it kosher
That he ate it

phrases.english: And let him answer him
such as where he ate it as a tereifa!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice of answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of נבילה as the answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טריפה would give a simpler answer, since its שחיטה might not count.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי מאיר: an unfit שחיטה still counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds like רבי מאיר. A שחיטה that does not make the animal permitted is still called שחיטה, so a טריפה would require ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר, who says: a שחיטה that is not fit is still called שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the טריפה answer would not work for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, slaughtering a טריפה still counts as שחיטה for ארבעה וחמשה. So in a טריפה case the שומר would pay ארבעה וחמשה, which does not fit the ברייתא. Only נבילה, with no שחיטה at all, works.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view רבי יוחנן follows here
A slaughter that does not make the animal fit to eat
It is still called (counts as) שחיטה

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Meir, who says:
a slaughter that is not fit is still called a slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by showing the טריפה answer does not fit רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא the speaker follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughtering a טריפה does not count, so it would explain why only כפל is paid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי מאיר, it counts, so a טריפה case would require ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Why not say it was a בן פקועה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not answer that the ox was a בן פקועה, which can be eaten without its own שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him answer instead: it is a case of a בן פקועה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one more possible answer: the animal was a בן פקועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן פקועה is a calf found inside its mother after the mother was slaughtered. If it needs no שחיטה of its own, he could eat it without slaughtering it. That would explain why only כפל is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal taken out of its mother's womb after the mother was slaughtered
Split open (the mother, from which the calf was taken)

phrases.english: And let him answer him
with a case of a ben pekua!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the choice of answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of נבילה as the answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בן פקועה can be eaten without שחיטה, which would be a simpler answer.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי מאיר: a בן פקועה needs שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds like רבי מאיר, who says a בן פקועה needs its own שחיטה. So eating it would again mean he slaughtered it, and the problem returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר, who says: a בן פקועה requires שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the בן פקועה answer would not work for רבי יוחנן. This leaves נבילה as the only answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a בן פקועה must be slaughtered before eating. So that case would again involve שחיטה and require ארבעה וחמשה. Only נבילה fits רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires (its own) שחיטה
Who says

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא as a case of a נבילה, with no שחיטה at all. The answers of טריפה and בן פקועה do not work for him, because he follows רבי מאיר. For רבי מאיר, slaughtering a טריפה counts as שחיטה, and a בן פקועה needs שחיטה.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Meir, who says:
a ben pekua requires slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 and confirms the answer of נבילה from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא the speaker follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בן פקועה needs no שחיטה, so it could explain why only כפל is paid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי מאיר, it needs שחיטה, so only the נבילה answer works.

steps.title: Why not answer with the case of 'Go out and give it to him'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not answer that בית דין had already told the thief 'צא תן לו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי יוחנן answer that this is a case where he stood in court and the judges told him: 'Go out and give it to him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one more answer that רבי יוחנן could have given and asks why he did not use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why this person does not pay ארבעה וחמשה. If בית דין had already ordered him to return the animal, he would have a different legal status and would not pay ארבעה וחמשה. So why did רבי יוחנן need the נבילה answer?

keyTerms.meaning: Stood trial in בית דין
'Go out and give it to him', a final court order
And let him answer it this way

phrases.english: And let him answer him
phrases.notes: He means: let רבי יוחנן give this answer to רבי חייא בר אבא.

phrases.english: that it is a case where he stood in judgment,
and they said to him: 'Go out, give it to him'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third in a series of 'why didn't he answer this way' questions, after טריפה and בן פקועה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's choice of the נבילה answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another simple case exists in which he would not pay ארבעה וחמשה, so why choose this one?

steps.title: רבא's rule: a court order turns a thief into a robber
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that after 'צא תן לו' the thief is a גזלן and does not pay ארבעה וחמשה. After 'חייב אתה ליתן לו' he is still a גנב and does pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא said: if they told him 'Go out, give it to him', and he slaughtered or sold it, he is exempt. Why? Once the court decided his case, if he slaughtered or sold it he is a robber, and a robber does not pay four or five. If they told him 'You are obligated to give it to him', and he slaughtered or sold it, he is liable. Why? As long as his case was not finally decided, he is still a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's ruling to show that the suggested answer in the last step really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא separates two kinds of court statements. 'צא תן לו' is a final ruling, so keeping the animal after it counts as open robbery (גזלן), and a גזלן never pays ארבעה וחמשה. 'חייב אתה ליתן לו' is not yet final, so he keeps the status of a secret thief (גנב) and still pays.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber, who takes openly
A thief, who takes secretly
The court decided his case
'You are obligated to give it to him', a ruling that is not yet a final order

steps.confusionAlert: The two court phrases sound almost the same, but only 'צא תן לו' is a final order. That is the whole difference between paying and not paying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that a person's legal status can change from גנב to גזלן because of what בית דין says.

phrases.english: For Rava has said:
'Go out, give it to him,' and he slaughtered or sold it – he is exempt.
What is the reason?
Since the court has decided his matter,
and he slaughtered or sold it – he is a robber,
and a robber does not pay
fourfold or fivefold payment.
'You are obligated to give it to him,'
and he slaughtered or sold it – he is liable.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: As long as the matter has not been finally decided for him,
he is still a thief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the premise of the question in step 15
steps.raayaObject: That a thief who was told 'צא תן לו' does not pay ארבעה וחמשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling separating 'צא תן לו' from 'חייב אתה ליתן לו'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן just picked one answer out of several
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there were several possible answers, such as a partner who slaughtered without the other partner knowing, and רבי יוחנן simply chose one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: by your logic, let him also answer that it was a partner who slaughtered without his fellow partner knowing! Rather, he just chose one out of two or three possible answers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing out that other answers also existed, and רבי יוחנן did not have to list all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questioner assumed that רבי יוחנן's answer had to be the only possible one. The reply shows that even more answers existed, like the partner case. So picking the נבילה case does not mean he rejected the others.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning
A partner
Without his fellow's knowledge
He chose one out of two or three

steps.whatToRemember: An אמורא who gives one answer is not saying it is the only answer. He may simply have chosen one out of several good ones.

phrases.english: They say:
And according to your reasoning,
let him answer him with the case of a partner
who slaughtered without his fellow's knowledge!
phrases.notes: This is another known case where the thief does not pay four or five.

phrases.english: Rather, he took one out of two or three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 (the 'צא תן לו' suggestion). The earlier טריפה and בן פקועה questions were already answered in steps 12 and 14 by pointing to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the assumption that the answer given had to be the only possible one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוחנן gave the נבילה answer, he must have rejected every other answer
steps.terutzMaskana: Several answers were possible, and he simply chose one

steps.title: A false claim of theft about a lost item brings double payment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that someone who falsely claims a lost item he found was stolen from him pays כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who claims that a thief stole a lost item pays double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related ruling from רבי יוחנן about the false claim of theft (טוען טענת גנב).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we discussed a שומר who falsely claims theft. Here the person is a finder of a lost item. רבי יוחנן says that he too pays כפל if he lies and says it was stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: One who falsely claims that a thief stole the item
A lost item
Double payment

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who makes the claim of a thief about a lost item,
phrases.notes: He found something lost, and when the owner asked for it back, he lied and said it was stolen from him.

phrases.english: pays double payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling from the same speakers, on the same topic of טוען טענת גנב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder who falsely claims a lost item was stolen pays כפל

steps.title: The source: 'for any lost item'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק about כפל, which mentions 'כל אבדה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because it is written: 'For any lost item about which he will say.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק that is the source for רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that teaches the כפל payment for a false theft claim also mentions a lost item. This shows that the כפל law applies to a finder who lies, not only to a regular שומר.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
'For any lost item about which he will say'

phrases.english: What is the reason?
As it is written:
'For any lost item about which he will say.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 18
steps.raayaObject: That a finder who falsely claims theft pays כפל

steps.title: A ברייתא: a minor's deposit creates no claim
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל quotes a ברייתא. It learns from the פסוקים that a deposit given by a קטן is meaningless, even if he makes the claim after he grows up. The giving and the claim must both happen when he is an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל challenged רבי חייא בר אבא using a ברייתא. The פסוק says 'If a man gives', so a minor's giving counts for nothing. That covers a case where he gave and claimed while still a minor. What if he gave as a minor and claimed as an adult? The פסוק says 'the matter of both of them shall come before the judges', which means the giving and the claim must be equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל is setting up an attack on the ruling from Step 18. Here he only quotes the ברייתא he will use. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns two things. From the word 'אִישׁ' it learns that a minor's deposit is not a legal deposit. From 'דְּבַר שְׁנֵיהֶם' it learns that even claiming later as an adult does not help, because the giving and the claim must both be done as an adult. This shows that the giving matters, and that is the point רבי אבא בר ממל will use.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
A minor, who has no legal standing in many areas
Giving, here the handing over of a deposit
A claim, here demanding the deposit back
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel raised an objection
to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
"If a man gives"
the giving of a minor is nothing.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא קָטָן,
phrases.english: And I only know the case where he gave it when he was a minor
and claimed it when he was a minor;
if he gave it when he was a minor
and claimed it when he was an adult, from where do we know?
The verse teaches:
"The matter of both of them shall come before the judges"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:8. Here הָאֱלֹהִים means the judges.

phrases.english: only when the giving and the claim
are equal, as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא in order to challenge the כפל ruling about a lost item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deposit given by a קטן creates no claim, even if he claims as an adult. The giving and the claim must both happen when he is an adult.

steps.title: Why isn't a minor's deposit treated like a lost item?
steps.stepSummary: If a finder pays כפל even though the owner never handed him the item, then a minor's deposit should also make the bailee liable, just like a lost item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is true that a finder pays כפל, then a minor's deposit should also be like a lost item!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the actual question comes. If giving is not needed for a lost item, why does the ברייתא say a minor's giving ruins the case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a lost item, nobody gave anything to the finder, yet he still pays כפל. So the act of giving should not be needed. Then a minor's useless 'giving' should not matter either, and the bailee should still pay.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so, meaning 'if your ruling is true'
A lost item

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if a finder really pays כפל, as in Step 18.

phrases.english: let it also be like a lost item!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 20 against the ruling of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling, reported by רבי חייא בר אבא, that a finder who falsely claims theft pays כפל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lost item shows that giving is not required for כפל. So a minor's deposit, where the giving does not count, should also lead to payment. The ברייתא says it does not.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about an item eaten while the owner was a minor
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the bailee ate the item while the owner was still a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he ate it while the owner was a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא defends the ruling by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that the minor handed it over. The problem is that the item was eaten while the owner was still a minor and had no legal standing, so no claim ever started. That fits with a lost item, where giving is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A way of narrowing a source to a specific case
He ate it, meaning he used up the deposit

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, what are we dealing with?
Such as where he ate it when he was a minor.
phrases.notes: The one who ate it is the bailee. The one who was still a minor is the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא frees the bailee because a minor's giving does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא frees the bailee because the item was eaten while the owner was a minor.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have said 'eating', not 'giving'
steps.stepSummary: If eating as an adult would make him pay, the ברייתא should have said that the eating and the claim must be equal, not the giving and the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he ate it when the owner was an adult, what then? Would he really pay? If so, instead of teaching 'only when the giving and the claim are equal', it should teach 'only when the eating and the claim are equal'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל pushes back on the answer by pointing to the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer means the deciding moment is the eating, not the giving. But the ברייתא clearly says 'נְתִינָה', giving. So the wording seems to go against the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching
Let it teach, meaning it should have said
Eating, here using up the deposit

phrases.english: But when he is an adult, what?
Indeed, would he pay?
If so, instead of teaching:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא נְתִינָה וּתְבִיעָה שָׁוִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: "only when the giving and the claim are equal as one,"
let it teach:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא אֲכִילָה וּתְבִיעָה שָׁוִין כְּאֶחָד!
phrases.english: "only when the eating and the claim are equal as one"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מַאי, הָכִי נָמֵי דִּמְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 22 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about an item eaten while the owner was a minor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating is the deciding moment, the ברייתא should have said 'אֲכִילָה', not 'נְתִינָה'.

steps.title: Change the wording of the ברייתא to 'eating'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says the ברייתא should indeed be read as 'the eating and the claim must be equal'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Teach it as 'only when the eating and the claim are equal'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא agrees with the point about the wording and simply changes the text of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking for a new answer, he fixes the wording so the ברייתא matches his explanation. Now the ברייתא no longer shows that giving is required, so the ruling about a lost item stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it as, meaning read the text this way

phrases.english: He said to him: Teach:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא אֲכִילָה וּתְבִיעָה שָׁוִין כְּאֶחָד.
phrases.english: "only when the eating and the claim are equal as one."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 23 by changing the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says 'נְתִינָה', so giving seems to be the deciding moment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading is 'אֲכִילָה', so eating is the deciding moment.

steps.title: רב אשי: a lost item came from someone with understanding
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently: the cases are not alike. A lost item came from an owner with legal understanding, but a minor's deposit did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: They are not alike. A lost item comes through the power of a person with understanding. This one does not come through the power of a person with understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second, different answer to the קשיא of Step 21, without changing the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי keeps the ברייתא's word 'נְתִינָה'. He explains that with a lost item, the item came from an adult owner even though he did not hand it over. With a minor's deposit, the item came from someone without legal understanding, so there is no claim. That is why the two cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not comparable
A person with legal understanding, such as an adult
Through the power of, coming from

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the challenge from a minor's deposit. רבי חייא בר אבא reads the ברייתא as being about eating while the owner was a minor. רב אשי says a lost item came from a בֶּן דַּעַת, and a minor's deposit did not.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is not comparable;
a lost item comes
through the power of a person with understanding,
but this one does not come
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the deposit given by a minor.

phrases.english: through the power of a person with understanding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the קשיא of Step 21, instead of the answer in Steps 22-24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the cases are different (לָא דָּמֵי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lost item and a minor's deposit are alike, since neither involves a valid act of giving.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lost item came from a בֶּן דַּעַת, so there is a claim. A minor's deposit did not, so there is no claim.

steps.title: A false thief claim only makes him liable if he admits part
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: a שומר who falsely claims a thief stole the deposit is not liable unless he denies part of the claim and admits part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a person who falsely claims that a thief stole a deposit is not liable until he denies part of the claim and admits part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי יוחנן about a שומר who falsely says a deposit was stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we picture a שומר who denies everything with a false טענת גנב. רבי יוחנן says that a complete denial is not enough to make him liable for the oath and כפל. He is only liable if he admits part and denies part.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim 'a thief stole it,' said by a שומר about an item he was watching
A deposit, an item given to someone to watch
Denies part of the claim
Admits part of the claim
Double payment, the penalty paid by a thief

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not liable' here does not mean the false claimer is innocent. It means the special oath-and-כפל process of the תורה does not apply unless there is a partial admission.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who makes a thief claim about a deposit,
phrases.notes: He is lying when he says a thief stole the item he was watching.

phrases.english: is not liable
until he denies part
and admits part.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new related ruling from the same speaker, רבי חייא בר אבא, who appeared in the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר's false טענת גנב makes him liable only when he denies part of the claim and admits part.

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a partial admission is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוחנן's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requirement of a partial admission is surprising, so the גמרא asks for a source. The next step will point to a word in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A standard request for a source or logic

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring a partial admission.

steps.title: The source: 'this is it'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'כי הוא זה' ('this is it'), which describes a person admitting to part of the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'that this is it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule comes from the words 'כי הוא זה' in the פסוק about a שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'this is it' means pointing to one part and admitting it. So the פסוק describes a person who admits part of the claim and denies the rest. That is when the oath and כפל apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק, a verse
'That this is it,' words that show a partial admission

steps.whyThisMatters: This same phrase is the well-known source for the oath of מודה במקצת. Here it is applied to a false thief claim.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
"That this is it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'כי הוא זה' show that the פסוק is talking about a partial admission.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר יוסף disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן's rule disagrees with רבי חייא בר יוסף and starts to quote him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי חייא בר יוסף, for רבי חייא בר יוסף said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says another אמורא holds differently and begins to quote him. This line only sets up his view; his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet in this line. The גמרא is flagging that the partial-admission requirement is disputed. The opposing view is spelled out at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees, a note that two rulings argue with each other

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef,
for Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a view that argues with רבי יוחנן's rule from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבי חייא בר יוסף's opposing view; its content follows on the next amud.
